key_insight: Routing codes are a new qLDPC family that keeps high encoding rates while making non-local couplings shorter, less connected, and fully parallel.
engineering_relevance: They are designed to fit real hardware better by eliminating wiring crossings in superconducting multilayers and simplifying atom-movement scheduling in neutral-atom arrays.
method: Construct explicit routing-code instances with rates comparable to bivariate bicycle codes.
Reduce qubit connectivity and shorten non-local coupling length.
Make all non-local couplings mutually parallel to support hardware-friendly layouts.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations show weight-7 routing codes can cut physical qubit overhead by about 8× versus surface codes at the same logical error rate.
watch_item: The main challenge is whether the code family can be realized with low-overhead control, fabrication, and decoding at scale in actual hardware.
paper_title: Routing Codes: High-Rate Quantum LDPC Codes with Short, Parallel Non-Local Connectivity
